item.description:
An AI engineering and evaluation challenge built for real-world impact.

  • 2 tracks
  • Virtual build phase
  • ₹10 Lakh prize pool
  • Grand Finale in New Delhi

The Innodata AI Hackathon is a nationwide AI engineering challenge, hosted by Innodata and powered by Hack2skill.

This isn’t your average app-building event. Teams build, test and benchmark next-generation AI systems, from synthetic data generators to automated testing pipelines that reveal what frontier models can really do.

As Innodata advances as a global AI-native company, we’re inviting India’s top AI/ML talent, developers and campus innovators to solve real-world AI engineering problems, with expert mentorship along the way.

  • Build

    Reusable pipelines that generate evaluation tasks and data.

  • Test

    Verifiable checks that frontier models can’t shortcut.

  • Benchmark

    Measure how frontier AI models really perform.

Two tracks. One goal: tests that AI models can’t shortcut.

Pick a track and build a reusable pipeline.

  • ✓Working, repeatable prototype
  • </>Any language, AI credits & tools
  • ↑Code, samples, evidence & demo
01
Track 1

Coding Task Factory

Problem statement

Using a supplied working software repository and task interface ↗, your team will build one reusable strategy for generating realistic feature-development tasks suitable for evaluating AI coding systems.

Each task package should contain clear, achievable requirements, a reference implementation, and tests that verify the new feature while protecting existing functionality. Packages must identify their starting repository version and follow the supplied task interface ↗.

Reference implementations and tests must work with the repository’s language, framework, dependencies, and execution environment. Validation evidence should show that implementations satisfy the requirements, feature tests detect missing or incorrect behavior, and regression checks protect existing functionality.

Supplied repositories
pallets/click ↗ colinhacks/zod ↗ open-source-parsers/jsoncpp ↗
The big question

How can we automatically create realistic software-development tasks that are clear, solvable, and reliably testable?

In short: turn a real codebase into new, testable coding tasks that fairly challenge AI coding systems.

Read moreShow less What you’ll build, how to stand out and what you’ll submit

What you’ll build

  • Clear, achievable requirements for a new feature
  • A reference implementation that runs in the repo’s stack
  • Feature tests plus regression checks for existing code
  • Packages tagged to their starting repo version

How to stand out

  • Prove each implementation meets its requirements
  • Show tests catch missing or incorrect behaviour
  • Vary behaviour, rules or interactions, not just names
  • Meaningful variation beats a high task count

What you’ll submit

  • A reusable task-generation pipeline
  • Sample task packages
  • Validation evidence: tests, runs and results
  • A live demo generating and validating a package

Example

A shopping-cart app gets a generated task to add discount codes with eligibility rules and spending thresholds, plus tests that prove it works.

Great fit if you enjoy

  • Extending existing codebases
  • Automating with model APIs
  • Writing testable requirements
  • Testing & debugging
  • Evaluating AI coding systems

Code-generation or AI-evaluation experience helps, but strong programming fundamentals matter most.

02
Track 2

Visual Task Factory

Problem statement

Your team will choose an image family and visual-understanding problem with meaningful practical impact. Build an automated pipeline that generates synthetic images, questions about those images, and verifiable reference answers.

Explain the application your chosen problem supports, why errors matter, and how your synthetic examples represent its visual challenges. Teams choose their image family, application domain, and generation approach.

Each task must require visual understanding, provide sufficient image evidence to answer the question, and include a reliable method for checking the answer. Explain how reference answers are established and validated independently of the model being evaluated. Use the generated tasks to evaluate advanced multimodal models and investigate their strengths and weaknesses.

The big question

Which visual capabilities matter most in real-world applications, and how can we reliably test whether advanced AI models possess them?

In short: create images and questions with answers you already know, then test how well top AI models really “see”.

Read moreShow less What you’ll build, how to stand out and what you’ll submit

What you’ll build

  • Pick an image family and a real-world visual problem
  • Generate synthetic images and questions about them
  • Reference answers checked without the tested model
  • An evaluation of advanced multimodal models

How to stand out

  • Every question needs genuine visual understanding
  • Each image holds enough evidence to answer
  • Vary visual relationships and reasoning, not just count
  • Explain why errors matter in the real application

What you’ll submit

  • A reusable generation and evaluation pipeline
  • Sample tasks with validation evidence
  • Findings on model strengths and weaknesses
  • A demo where scoring separates right from wrong

Example

Your code draws a bar chart, so it already knows which bar is tallest and can check every model’s answer.

Great fit if you enjoy

  • Image generation
  • Structured data
  • Logic, algorithms & testing
  • Designing experiments

Experience with computer vision or synthetic data helps, but curiosity and careful reasoning matter most.
